title: The Role of Carbenicillin as an Inhibitor of the Biofilm Regulator CsgD in Salmonella Typhimurium.
authors: Narimisa, Negar; Khoshbayan, Amin; Masjedian Jazi, Faramarz; Razavi, Shabnam
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选靶向沙门氏菌生物膜调控因子CsgD（转录因子）的抗生素，并实验验证其抑制效果，虽涉及TF-DNA相关调控但未聚焦DNA结合机制，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium, a major foodborne pathogen, forms biofilms that enhance its environmental persistence and resistance to antibiotics, presenting significant public health challenges. The CsgD protein, a key transcriptional regulator, orchestrates biofilm formation by regulating curli fimbriae and cellulose production. This study aimed to identify and evaluate potential CsgD inhibitors to disrupt S. Typhimurium biofilms using a combination of computational and experimental methodologies. Molecular docking was performed to screen 145 FDA-approved antibiotics from DrugBank against the CsgD protein. Carbenicillin, identified as a top candidate, was further analyzed through 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to assess the stability of the carbenicillin-CsgD complex. Experimental evaluations determined the minimum biofilm inhibitory concentration (MBIC), and minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) of carbenicillin against S. Typhimurium isolates. Biofilm structure and curli production were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Congo red agar assays, respectively. Molecular docking revealed carbenicillin's high binding affinity to CsgD. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the structural stability of the carbenicillin-CsgD complex. Experimental assays established MBIC and MBEC at 1 and 4 mug/mL, respectively. SEM analysis showed morphological changes and disrupted biofilm architecture at 0.5-1 mug/mL carbenicillin, while Congo red agar assays demonstrated dose-dependent suppression of curli production. Carbenicillin exhibits significant potential as a CsgD-targeted anti-biofilm agent, providing a foundation for novel therapeutic strategies to combat S. Typhimurium infections and address their public health burden.
abstract_zh: 鼠伤寒沙门氏菌（Salmonella Typhimurium）是一种主要的食源性病原体，其形成的生物膜增强了其在环境中的持久性和对抗生素的耐药性，构成了重大的公共卫生挑战。CsgD蛋白作为关键转录调控因子，通过调控卷曲菌毛（curli fimbriae）和纤维素（cellulose）的产生来协调生物膜形成。本研究旨在利用计算与实验相结合的方法，识别并评估潜在的CsgD抑制剂，以破坏鼠伤寒沙门氏菌的生物膜。通过分子对接（molecular docking）对DrugBank中145种FDA批准的抗生素进行筛选，以靶向CsgD蛋白。碳苄青霉素（Carbenicillin）被鉴定为最佳候选药物，并通过100 ns分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟进一步分析碳苄青霉素-CsgD复合物的稳定性。实验评估确定了碳苄青霉素对鼠伤寒沙门氏菌分离株的最低生物膜抑制浓度（MBIC）和最低生物膜根除浓度（MBEC）。利用扫描电子显微镜（SEM）和刚果红琼脂实验分别观察生物膜结构和卷曲菌毛产生情况。分子对接结果显示碳苄青霉素对CsgD具有高结合亲和力。分子动力学模拟证实了碳苄青霉素-CsgD复合物的结构稳定性。实验测定MBIC和MBEC分别为1和4 μg/mL。SEM分析显示，在0.5-1 μg/mL碳苄青霉素浓度下，生物膜结构发生形态变化并被破坏，而刚果红琼脂实验则表明卷曲菌毛产生呈剂量依赖性抑制。碳苄青霉素作为靶向CsgD的抗生物膜剂展现出显著潜力，为应对鼠伤寒沙门氏菌感染及其公共卫生负担的新型治疗策略奠定了基础。
